question: A dealer purchased a laptop for ₹99,000. He allows a discount of 37% on its marked price and still gains 40%. Find the marked price of the laptop.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The direct ratio between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) can be calculated as (100 − D%) : (100 + P%).

CP : MP = (100 − 37) : (100 + 40)

CP : MP = 63 : 140 = 9 : 20

Here, 9 units → ₹99,000

1 unit → ₹11,000 ⇒ 20 units → ₹2,20,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,20,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹99,000

Discount (D%) = 37%

Profit (P%) = 40%

**Formula Used:**

MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100 = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100

 
 
 CP ₹99,000 SP ₹1,38,600 MP ₹2,20,000 
 + 40% Profit 
 − 37% Discount CP : MP = (100 − D%) : (100 + P%) 

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = CP × [(100 + P%) ÷ (100 − D%)]

⇒ MP = 99000 × [(100 + 40) ÷ (100 − 37)]

⇒ MP = 99000 × (140 ÷ 63)

⇒ MP = 99000 × (20 ÷ 9)

⇒ MP = 11000 × 20

⇒ MP = 220000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,20,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and Cost Price Relation

The direct shortcut ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is derived from the Selling Price equations: CP ÷ MP = (100 − D%) ÷ (100 + P%).

Selling Price (SP)

Selling Price acts as the bridging link connecting Cost Price and Marked Price. Hence, SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of x% and y% are allowed on a product, the effective single discount is calculated as (x + y − xy ÷ 100)%.
